scores.evidence: There are two can-do objectives. o3 is evaluate (「判断できる」) and o4 is create (「作り…直せる」). o3 is tested by pq1 (inline, 買い物メモ) and pq2 (exam, ジム記録), with pq0 as an ungraded predict. o4 is tested by pq3 (レシピ帳, missing Must) and pq4 (AI-guessed 「使う人」). Every item uses a new context. The create level is also assessed by practice-checklist.

hook-b1 is a concrete 3-sentence scene (「気づけば、6つ全部をMustにしていました。」) followed by an ungraded predict question, pq0, that leads into o3. However, the problem shown is over-scoping, while pq0 asks how to split work with the AI. Also, option b is the only non-extreme choice, so the answer is easy to guess rather than predict.

The prerequisite (第2章) is stated, and hook-b1 recalls 「第2章の家計簿アプリと同じ流れで」. practice-recap restates MoSCoW, and the glossary has 壁打ち, MoSCoW and 1枚企画書. But 「Must」 (hook-b1) and 「MoSCoWの4つ」 (pq0 a) appear before practice-recap defines them. In p-interview, the term is used once before its gloss sentence.

Lint is clean (0 warnings), and the brief reports a body of about 2,038 characters with no new terms. But the practice section holds 10 blocks. Steps p-interview, p-moscow and p-plan say 「下の…依頼文」, yet all three prompts come after all six steps. The learner has to scroll back and forth, and the checklist the steps point to comes last.

This is a practice lesson split from vibe-ch2, which holds the full 家計簿 worked example, so having no concept or example segment is justified. Within this lesson there are partial faded examples: the var hint for 自分の分け方 shows a full 家計簿 sort, and the club-app model in practice-prompt.expect gives 「理由の例」 and the AI's remark. The step blocks themselves give what to do and an expected result, but rarely why.

The single content section has one inline check, pq1, an evaluate-level item in a new context with feedback on every wrong option, so density is met. But the right option (「なくても目的は果たせるので」) echoes the AI remark in the stem. There is also no inline retrieval for o4 before the exam.

All four misconceptions in the brief appear as distractors with feedback of at most 2 sentences. 「AIに任せる」 is pq0 a and pq1 c. 「便利・迷う→Must」 is pq0 c, pq1 b and pq2 c. 「Won'tは消す」 is pq1 d and pq2 d. 「AIの推測をそのまま使う」 is pq4 a. Each feedback names the misconception and corrects it, e.g. 「便利さは、Mustかどうかの物差しではありません。」

practice-flow is a 4-node process diagram whose labels match the plan's screen flow (イベントの作成 → イベント一覧 → 出欠の入力 → 参加人数の一覧). It has a takeaway caption (「Mustの画面だけで、作成から人数の確認まで通る」), an alt, and EN labels. There are no images.

This is a transfer task on the learner's own app. All six steps have expect, hint and troubleshoot, which gives a hint ladder. There are model answers in practice-prompt.expect and practice-prompt-plan.expect, in disclosures that practice-tip points to, plus a 7-item self-check (practice-checklist), including pc-flow.

summary-points (4 points) comes after the exam. summary-next has a reflection prompt (「AIの指摘のうち、受け入れなかったものはありましたか？」) and the next step (ch3/ch4). There are 4 flashcards that ask for retrieval, plus askTutor suggestions.

The MoSCoW meanings in practice-recap and check-quiz are cited to abc-moscow, the interview prompt is cited to cc-best-practices, and the AI-behaviour claims are hedged (「埋まることがあります」, 「書き始めたら」). One inaccuracy: summary-next says 「第4章でAIに画面を作ってもらうときは、この1枚企画書を一緒に渡せます」, but the current vibe-ch4 prompt builds a page from an attached image and never uses a plan.

Body text, step expects and summary are in です・ます, warm and non-pressuring (「思いつかなければ…試しましょう」). There are no banned phrases, and the terms Must/Should/Could/Won't and 1枚企画書 are used consistently. Flashcard backs and checklist labels use plain form, which is acceptable for those block types.

Every learner-facing string has jp and en (none missing), including the Mermaid labels, caption and alt. The EN reads naturally. practice-tip's EN quotes the reader's real EN disclosure label, "What a good answer looks like".

niceToHave: practice-steps / prompts: put each prompt right after the step that uses it, or add the prompt title and a step number to each step, so learners don't scroll past 4 later steps to find 「下の…依頼文」.

hook-predict: make the options parallel so b is not the only balanced choice. For example, make d 「自分で分けたあと、AIに足りない機能だけ挙げてもらう」, a near-miss that skips the reasons. Or tie pq0 more directly to the 6-Must problem in hook-b1.
hook-predict pq0 a feedback: 「AIは分けられても、自分の目的にとって何が必須かは決められません」 conflicts with pq1, where the AI correctly judges a Must against the goal. Suggest 「AIの分け方は材料になりますが、何を最初の版に入れるかを決めるのは自分です。」
summary-next: the current vibe-ch4 prompt builds from an attached image and does not use a plan. Soften the sentence to 「この先、AIに画面を作ってもらうときに…」, or confirm with the owner when ch4 is reworked.
o3 says 「Must以外も含めて」, but no graded item separates Should from Could. Consider a Could option in pq2, or a flashcard on Should vs Could.
o4 has no inline check. A short inline item after practice-prompt-plan (e.g. spot the missing heading in a sample plan) would give o4 the inline-plus-exam pair the contract recommends.
hook-b1 / pq0: write MoSCoW as [[MoSCoW]], linked to the glossary, on first use in the hook, since practice-recap comes later.
summary: Biggest strength: the practice is a real transfer task with a hint and troubleshoot ladder on every step, club-app model answers, and a checklist that the exam items (pq2–pq4) test in new contexts. Every distractor encodes one of the brief's four misconceptions. Most useful fix: put each prompt next to the step that uses it, and make the hook's predict options parallel so the answer is not obvious.
